title: quantile telemetry orchestration and dashboarding for per-route/model/region SLOs
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Background: We need first-class, per-route/model/region p95 and p99 visibility plus tokens/sec rollups and an automated regression detection pipeline. Current rollups are coarse and do not support fine-grained attribution by model variant + region simultaneously, which hinders SLO debugging and increases MTTI for regressions.

Goals:
- Instrument request paths to emit quantile-friendly telemetry (histogram/t-digest metadata) with tags: route, model_id, model_variant, region, instance_type, customer_tier.
- Record tokens/sec counters and sequence-length distributions per route/model/region.
- Build a streaming rollup pipeline that computes per-minute and hourly p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec aggregates with bounded storage cost.
- Expose a Grafana dashboard and an internal Redwood Console view for per-route/model/region quantiles with drilldowns and comparison timespans (baseline vs current).
- Implement regression detection that flags statistically significant p95/p99 shifts for a route+model+region and opens a ticket automatically when thresholds are exceeded.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Aggregation format: we will emit compressed histograms (tdigest) at the edge for each request window and aggregate them in the stream. This balances precision for tail quantiles and storage cost. We evaluated using fixed-bucket Prometheus histograms but they caused high cardinality and poor p99 accuracy on long-tailed traffic.
- Cardinality control: limit tag cardinality by mapping instance-level tags to coarser buckets (instance_class) and by synchronizing model_variant tag values via a canonical registry. Implement TTLed dynamic-tag fallback for unknown variants.
- Storage: store per-minute rollups for 30 days and hourly rollups for 365 days in ClickHouse using compact tdigest blobs. Raw per-request traces remain in short-term trace store (7 days).
- Regression detection: use a two-stage approach: 1) statistical test (Welch's t-test on bootstrapped tdigest samples) to detect shifts; 2) effect-size thresholding (relative increase at p95/p99) plus minimum sample-volume guardrails. We prefer pragmatic detection with low false positives over hyper-sensitive alerts.

Implementation tasks:
- Telemetry schema changes: add field quantile_histogram and tokens_emitted to request event proto; update SDKs to populate when sampling enabled.
- Edge SDK rollout: phased enable by region with 1% traffic sampling to validate payload sizes.
- Stream pipeline: new aggregation job in ingestion cluster (kafka -> flink -> clickhouse). Include dedup logic for retries.
- Dashboard: Grafana dashboard JSON + Redwood Console integration for drilldowns and compare periods; include heatmap view for token/sec vs tail latency.
- Load harness: extend the existing load harness to synthesize mixed-sequence lengths and model splits; measure tokens/sec and p95/p99 under target QPS patterns.
- Regression engine: a lambda that consumes rollups and emits findings to monitoring+Linear (auto-open) with context (sampled traces, recent deploys).

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 and p99 metrics available by route+model+region in Grafana for at least 30 days of simulated data.
- Regression detector fires on synthetic 20% tail latency increase and creates ENG ticket with links to traces and load test run.
- No >10% payload size increase for telemetry on sampled traffic.
- Dashboards include tokens/sec and sequence-length distribution panels with ability to compare arbitrary time ranges.

Risk and mitigations:
- High cardinality -> enforce tag normalization and hack fallback to aggregated buckets.
- Storage growth -> retention policy and compacting tdigest blobs; monitor ClickHouse ingestion invoices.
- False-positive alerts -> tune effect-size and minimum-sample thresholds during ramp.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement telemetry proto and SDK changes behind a feature flag; run internal canary for one region.
2) Deploy stream aggregation job in staging; replay 7 days of production traffic to validate quantiles.
3) Publish Grafana dashboard for staging; iterate with PM/DS/SE.
4) Enable regression detector in read-only mode (notifications only) for 1 week; refine thresholds.
5) Flip to active ticketing and extend sampling to production with controlled ramp to 20% traffic.

Metrics to track for this ticket: tokens/sec estimation error vs ground truth, p95/p99 stability on baseline, false-positive rate of regression detector, ClickHouse storage delta, telemetry payload overhead.
